articles.title: Wired charging, wireless charging and battery care
articles.path: USB-C / compatible wireless charger → Settings → Battery
articles.purpose: Recognize charging status and investigate heat or slow charging. A rated maximum does not mean every session reaches that power.
prerequisites: Compatible, undamaged charger, cable or wireless charging pad
Dry device and ports
Remove metal objects and incompatible cases before wireless charging
steps: Wired: connect an undamaged cable to USB-C and a compatible charger, then check for the on-screen charging indicator.
Wireless: align the center of the phone’s back as directed by the charging-pad instructions, keep it in contact and check for charging status. The alignment position has not been tested.
Open Settings → Battery, note the charge level and status, then check later whether the charge level increases.
Stop charging if there is overheating, an unusual smell, swelling, liquid ingress or port damage, and contact a qualified repair service.
When finished, unplug by holding the connector rather than pulling the cable. Lift the phone off the pad to end wireless charging.
options: Shows the battery percentage in the status bar

Measurement equipment and recorded conditions are required to claim rated charging performance
articles.result: A charging indicator should appear and the charge level should rise. Charging power and wireless charging were not measured in this session.
articles.undo: Unplug the charger or remove the phone from the pad. Allow it to cool naturally if temperature is a concern.
trouble: No charging: try a known working outlet, cable and charger
Wireless charging fails: check alignment, metal objects and the case
Slow charging: check temperature, current workload and charger negotiation; the animation alone cannot diagnose a fault
articles.limits: The official specifications checked on 2026-10-14 list 5000 mAh and up to 33 W wired / 15 W wireless charging. An older alpha PDF lists 5010 mAh and IP67, which conflict with the current public page; those older specifications are not used here.
